Image 1: Twelve-panel storyboard reference, used for the overall shot structure, shot sizes, and camera-movement rhythm. Read it from left to right and from top to bottom; panel N is Shot N. It is a line-art sketch: do not adopt its sketch style, black outlines, white background, panel borders or drawn faces.
Image 2: Reference of Garden of the wedding venue, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, a rendered set, not live action. Use it only for the room's layout, the furniture's positions and the light's direction; do not reference its visual content. It contains no people.
Image 3: Reference of Garden of the wedding venue, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 4: Reference of Garden of the wedding venue, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 5: Reference of Garden of the wedding venue, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 6: Reference of Garden of the wedding venue, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 7: Blocking reference of the segment's start: the same place with these people in their places, used only for where each person is and which way they face; take faces and outfits from each subject's own image. It is a line-art diagram: do not adopt its outlines or white background.
Image 8: Subject 1 (Natalie, look S1) character appearance reference.
Image 9: Subject 2 (Sebastian, look S2) character appearance reference.
Image 10: Subject 3 (George, look S1) character appearance reference.
Image 11: Subject 4 (Officiant) character appearance reference.
Image 12: Subject 5 (Cassie, look S1) character appearance reference.
Image 13: Subject 6 (Lauren, look S1) character appearance reference.
Image 14: Subject 7 (Guest 1) character appearance reference.
Image 15: Subject 8 (Guest 2) character appearance reference.
Image 16: Prop 1 (wedding-gift box) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 16.
Image 17: Prop 2 (bouquet) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 17.
[Subject settings]
Subject 1 (Natalie): Refer to Image 8. 25, the heroine; George's daughter from his first marriage, who agrees to marry Sebastian Klein to pay for her mother's dialysis. Outfit: look S1: An elegant, figure-fitted ivory-white satin bridal gown with thin spaghetti straps and a low sweetheart neckline. The sculpted bodice is fitted, and the skirt hugs her hips before flaring softly into a floor-length hem. A narrow pale-blue satin sash, her 'something blue', cinches the waist. A short sheer tulle veil is pinned at the back of her curls. Ivory satin pointed-toe heels. No jewellery. Signature colour: blue.
Subject 2 (Sebastian): Refer to Image 9. 30, the hero; the scorned illegitimate son of the Klein family, jailed for three days for reckless driving and secretly a billionaire running a plan. Outfit: look S2: A black slim-cut tuxedo jacket with satin lapels, a crisp white dress shirt, a black bow tie, black tuxedo trousers, black patent oxfords, a small white rose boutonnière and the steel-and-black wristwatch. Signature colour: black.
Subject 3 (George): Refer to Image 10. 55, Natalie's weak-willed father, head of the Quinn family, remarried to Lauren. Outfit: look S1: A charcoal-grey two-piece suit over a white dress shirt, a silver-grey silk tie, a pale-grey pocket square and black leather oxfords. Signature colour: grey.
Subject 4 (Officiant): Refer to Image 11. 58, the wedding officiant who marries Natalie and Sebastian. Outfit: A dark charcoal-black two-piece suit over a pale-blue dress shirt with a plain dark tie, a long cream-white satin officiant's stole draped over his shoulders and hanging down the front of the jacket, black leather oxfords and thin gold-framed reading glasses. He holds his hands clasped in front of him. Signature colour: white.
Subject 5 (Cassie): Refer to Image 12. 23, Natalie's spoiled stepsister, Lauren's daughter, who pushes Natalie into the marriage meant for her. Outfit: look S1: A scarlet-red satin bodycon cocktail dress with thin straps, a plunging neckline, a cinched waist and a high thigh slit on a short hem. Gold statement hoops, a gold cuff bracelet and gold strappy stilettos. No jacket. Signature colour: red.
Subject 6 (Lauren): Refer to Image 13. 50, Natalie's controlling stepmother, George's wife and Cassie's mother, who holds the family purse. Outfit: look S1: A knee-length lilac-purple fitted sheath dress with short sleeves and a round neck, nude heels, a pearl necklace, pearl studs and the same slim gold wristwatch. Signature colour: purple.
Subject 7 (Guest 1): Refer to Image 14. 25, a gossiping wedding guest. Outfit: A knee-length blush-pink fitted cocktail dress with short sleeves and a square neckline, a silver clutch, small silver earrings and nude block heels. Signature colour: pink.
Subject 8 (Guest 2): Refer to Image 15. 25, a gossiping wedding guest. Outfit: A knee-length mustard-yellow sleeveless A-line sundress with a fitted bodice and a round neck, small gold studs, a woven straw clutch and tan sandals. Signature colour: yellow.
Environment (Garden of the wedding venue): Refer to Images 2 to 6. Day, bright sunny garden light. High sunlight from the rose-bush side gives warm, soft highlights; the white drapes glow. Live sound: birdsong, leaves rustling, faint murmurs from the guests.
Do not swap the characters' appearances, clothing, actions, positions or dialogue.
[Subjects and relationships]
Only eight people appear throughout: Natalie, Sebastian, George, Officiant, Cassie, Lauren, Guest 1, and Guest 2.
[Blocking]
Refer to Images 2 to 6 for the room and Image 7 for the people's places. Camera on the aisle in front of the white wooden wedding arch, on the rose-bush side. Natalie, in her ivory bridal gown and short veil, stands under the centre of the arch, holding the one bouquet loosely at her waist and staring at Sebastian. Sebastian, in his black tuxedo, stands beside her under the arch on the boxwood-hedge side, facing her. George, in his charcoal suit, stands beside Natalie under the arch on the rose-bush side, facing down the aisle. The Officiant stands at the centre of the arch just behind the couple, hands clasped, facing down the aisle. Cassie, in her scarlet satin cocktail dress, stands at the head of the aisle a step in front of Natalie on the rose-bush side, holding the one empty white gift box with its lid off. Lauren, in her lilac sheath dress with a small handbag on her arm, stands at the head of the aisle against the front-row chair on the boxwood-hedge side. Two short rows of white folding chairs flank the petal aisle. Natalie's phone lies face up on the seat of the front-row chair on the rose-bush side. On the boxwood-hedge side of the lawn stands one small round white high cocktail table with one silver tray; Guest 1 stands at it on the arch side and Guest 2 on the aisle side, each holding a champagne flute, and Guest 1's pink phone is in the silver clutch under her arm.
[Overall style]
Photorealistic live-action short drama with cinematic lighting. Each character keeps the face and the outfit with its main colour from their reference image throughout. Use each character sheet only for that character: the face from the close-up on the right, the body and outfit from the turnaround on the left; do not render the sheet's layout, white background or multiple views. This segment has 9 lines, in this order: Cassie, Lauren, Natalie, Sebastian, Natalie, Officiant, Natalie, Sebastian, Officiant. Generate speech only from the lines in {} in the shot list, each spoken exactly once by its speaker; everyone else keeps their mouth naturally closed while listening, and a V.O. speaker keeps their mouth closed or is off screen. Follow the shot list below; do not add cuts or camera moves beyond it. Strictly adhere to the 180-degree rule: within a scene, characters keep their screen sides and the camera stays on one side of the axis. Seamless continuity of action, spatial matching and consistent actor blocking; cut on action. For dialogue prefer static shot-reverse-shot and over-the-shoulder shots, balanced with reaction shots and close-up inserts. Faces stable and clear, consistent with the reference images, with no resemblance to any real actor or actress. Normal human eyes. Natural anatomy and hands. Natural, fluid motion that follows the blocking; characters make subtle, natural movements. Characters, props and environment share one world with matched lighting. Each line ends naturally with breathing room and is never cut off. Authentic performances with micro-expressions. No BGM; generate only dialogue, environmental sounds and action sounds. No subtitles.
[Continuity]
Maintain continuity in the identities, number, appearance, clothing, relative heights, spatial positions, and eyelines of all the characters. The actions in the shot list occur strictly in sequence. Hands are anatomically correct.
[Strictly exclude]
added or missing characters, spatial jumps. malformed hands on the lapels, the bouquet or the gift box. subtitles or garbled text. Dialogue from the wrong character, multiple people speaking at once, repeated or missing lines, lip-sync errors and audio-visual desynchronization. The raw reference images (character sheets, setting plates) appearing as a frame of the video, and starting on a still frame of the setting reference. A fast zoom-in at the start, a fast pull-back at the end, unmotivated whip-pans, tilts, zooms and 360-degree orbits. Axis-crossing, jump cuts, frame skips, flicker and clipping. Face swaps, changes in age or clothing, sudden height shifts, added or missing characters, spatial jumps, and disordered action sequences; props popping in or vanishing, and duplicate characters except mirror reflections. Hand clipping, extra fingers, fused fingers, malformed hands. Subtitles, captions, watermarks and garbled writing; writing and logos other than those on a key prop's reference image, which are copied from it; a phone screen or paper that is not a key prop is shown from the back or out of focus. Black-and-white, monochrome, grayscale, desaturated visuals; hand-drawn, sketch, line art, illustration, comics, animation; storyboard frames, rough sketches, panel borders, gutters and grid layouts.
[Shot list] (12 shots, approximately 29 seconds)
When a previous-shot reference image is given, it is the moment this segment starts from: keep its people's positions, outfits, props and light, and continue from there. Shot 1 keeps its own camera, matching the image's framing only when it frames the same view; do not repeat that frame later.
Shot 1 (0-3s): [Wide shot, slow push in from the aisle toward the arch, eye-level, from the rose-bush side] Natalie, bouquet at her waist, faces Sebastian under the flower-hung arch, with George beside her on the rose-bush side and the Officiant behind them. Cassie, a step in front of Natalie, tips the empty white gift box toward her with a smirk; Lauren stands against the front-row chair on the hedge side, and Guest 1 and Guest 2 watch from the cocktail table by the hedge with their flutes. Dialogue (Cassie, in English, sugary and mocking): {Nothing. Just like your husband's bank account.}
Shot 2 (3-6s): [Medium shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, from the rose-bush side of the aisle] Lauren, leaning against the front-row chair on the hedge side, looks Natalie up and down and arches a brow; behind her, out of focus, Guest 1 and Guest 2 stand at the cocktail table with their flutes. Dialogue (Lauren, in English, icy drawl): {A rented dress and a broke groom. At least they match.}
Shot 3 (6-8s): [Medium close-up, clean single framed tight on face and shoulders, locked-off camera, eye-level] Natalie, under the arch, turns her head toward Lauren and holds her stepmother's eyes with a level, cold gaze. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, quiet and cutting): {You picked him.}
Shot 4 (8-11s): [Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot from behind Natalie's shoulder, eye-level] Sebastian, on the hedge side of the arch, leans slightly toward Natalie with a lazy, amused half-smile, the back of Natalie's veil in the foreground. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, low and teasing): {Don't worry. My family doesn't like me either.}
Shot 5 (11-13s): [Medium shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, Sebastian's shoulder at one frame edge and George's arm at the other] Natalie, bouquet still at her waist, looks up at Sebastian and a small smile breaks across her face. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, dry and warm): {Good. One less family to impress.}
Shot 6 (13-16s): [Medium shot, slight low angle, locked-off camera, the arch drapes framing him] The Officiant, hands clasped, looks from Natalie to Sebastian; their shoulders show at both frame edges. Dialogue (Officiant, in English, measured and ceremonial): {Natalie, Sebastian. Are you both ready to marry?}
Shot 7 (16-18s): [Close-up, clean single on her face, locked-off camera, eye-level] Natalie lifts her chin and gives a firm nod, her eyes steady. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, firm): {Yes.}
Shot 8 (18-20s): [Medium close-up, clean single, slow push in on Sebastian, eye-level] Sebastian glances past Natalie toward Cassie and Lauren at the head of the aisle, then back at her with a sly grin. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, lazy murmur): {Let's give them something to hate.}
Shot 9 (20-22s): [Medium shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, from the aisle on the rose-bush side] The Officiant opens his clasped hands toward the couple, with Natalie and Sebastian at the frame edges. Dialogue (Officiant, in English, warm and resonant): {Then I pronounce you married.}
Shot 10 (22-25s): [Medium shot, three-shot under the arch, handheld camera, eye-level] Sebastian offers Natalie his open hand. Natalie pushes the bouquet into George's hands beside her, ignores Sebastian's hand, grabs his satin lapels and pulls him close. <Fabric rustles>
Shot 11 (25-27s): [Close-up, slow orbit around the couple on the aisle side, starting on Natalie's profile and ending on Sebastian's, eye-level] Natalie and Sebastian share a brief kiss under the white roses, her hands still holding his lapels. <A few guests gasp softly>
Shot 12 (27-29s): [Medium shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, from the rose-bush side of the aisle] Cassie, in front of the arch on the rose-bush side, lowers the gift box and stares with her lips parted, and Lauren, against the front-row chair on the hedge side, stiffens.
At the end: Natalie and Sebastian stand close together, face to face, under the centre of the wedding arch, Natalie's hands lowering from his lapels, Sebastian on the boxwood-hedge side. George stands beside Natalie under the arch on the rose-bush side, holding the bouquet. The Officiant stands just behind the couple at the centre of the arch, facing down the aisle. Cassie stands at the head of the aisle a step in front of Natalie on the rose-bush side, holding the empty gift box. Lauren stands at the head of the aisle against the front-row chair on the boxwood-hedge side, her handbag on her arm. Natalie's phone lies face up on the seat of the front-row chair on the rose-bush side. Guest 1 (arch side) and Guest 2 (aisle side) stand at the one small round white high cocktail table on the boxwood-hedge side, each holding a champagne flute, Guest 1's phone in the clutch under her arm.

Image 18 is the first frame.
